answers.core:
Its essential feature if the user wants to create UI in a vertical script.
While some languages like Chinese or Japanese can be written and read horizontally, others like Mongolian Script cannot. And if its implemented for one language type, why not allow for others.
answers.workaround:
For Vertical left to right:
rotate the transform of the rich text label by -90 or -PI/2
set scale of the transform of the rich text label as (-1,1)
Using RichTextEffect
```gdscript
func _process_custom_fx(char_fx: CharFXTransform) -> bool:
	char_fx.transform=char_fx.transform.scaled_local(Vector2(1,-1))
	return true
```
Result: almost working except the line spacing is off due to flipping the text horizontally by the scale, and the spacing is either too narrow or too wide.

For Vertical right-to-left:
rotate the transform of the rich text label by -90 or -PI/2
Result: working

For Vertical left-to-right upright:
rotate the transform of the rich text label by -90 or -PI/2
set scale of the transform of the rich text label as (-1,1)
Using RichTextEffect
```gdscript
func _process_custom_fx(char_fx: CharFXTransform) -> bool:
	char_fx.transform=char_fx.transform.scaled_local(Vector2(1,-1))
	char_fx.transform=char_fx.transform.rotated_local(-PI/2)
	#to offset the font size
	char_fx.offset.y+= 100
	return true
```
Result: Top row isn't visible unless the x offset is set to the font size

For Vertical right-to-left upright:
rotate the transform of the rich text label by -90 or -PI/2
Using RichTextEffect
```gdscript
func _process_custom_fx(char_fx: CharFXTransform) -> bool:
	char_fx.transform=char_fx.transform.rotated_local(-PI/2)
	#to offset the font size
	char_fx.offset.y+= 100
	return true
```

Result: Top row isn't visible unless the x offset is set to the font size

title: More text direction options for vertical left to right and right to left
